newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Two Queensland credit unions plan to merge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Two Queensland credit unions plan to merge.

text.p: Two credit unions based in the state of Queensland will merge to form Australia's second largest credit union, they announced on Thursday.

THe boards of Credit Union Australia (CUA) Ltd and CPS credit Society Ltd have given unanimous support to the friendly merger, which would create an entity with assets of A$645 million, CUA chief executive Graham Olrich said in a statement.
The merger, which will be recommended to members during special general meetings expected to be held in March 1997, will make CUA the 4th largest Queensland-based financial institution.
"The merger will strengthen our ability to compete as an alternative to the banking sector," Olrich said.
"This is particularly critical as changes to industry regulations open the market to greater competition."
It was anticipated that, subject to approval, operations would commence on July 1, 1997, with the new entity to be known by the Credit Union Australia Limited name, the statement said.
The CUA's membership base would rise to over 150,000 following the merger, with 57 branches including three rxisting CPS braches in the state of Victoria.

"With the various mergers in the financial sector and the potential for more to occur following the Wallis Inquiry, our future is in strengthening our ability to be the preferred financial institution to meet the needs of our members," Orlich said.
